title: Nous Research in talks to raise $75M at reported $1.5B valuation as Hermes agent gains traction
summary: Nous Research, maker of the open-source Hermes AI agent, is reportedly in discussions to raise at least $75 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, according to TechCrunch. Robot Ventures would lead the round, with Union Square Ventures among the participating investors. The round has not closed; these figures represent current negotiation targets.
body:
Nous Research is in talks to raise at least $75 million in new funding at a reported $1.5 billion valuation, according to a TechCrunch report published July 13. The round has not closed. The figures reflect terms under negotiation, not a completed transaction.

Robot Ventures, which already backed the company in earlier rounds, would lead the raise. Union Square Ventures is among the participating investors. No closing timeline or formal term sheet is mentioned in available reporting.

Founded in 2023 by Jeffrey Quesnelle, Karan Malhotra, Ryan Teknium, and Shivani Mitra, Nous Research had previously raised approximately $70 million from Paradigm, Robot Ventures, North Island Ventures, OSS Capital, and angel investor Balaji Srinivasan. The $50 million Series A figure circulating in some aggregators is unverified secondary sourcing; TechCrunch's $70 million total is the primary figure here.

The company's main product is Hermes, an open-source AI agent built for task automation. Hermes integrates web search, code execution, and image understanding, and is designed to acquire new skills automatically. It supports deployment on desktop, virtual private servers, or the company's cloud infrastructure, with hosted tiers priced from $20 to $200 per month. The Hermes GitHub repository carries roughly 214,000 stars and 40,000 forks — figures cited in TechCrunch's reporting and not independently verified. Nous Research also develops specialized language models targeting coding and mathematics.

The company's agent offering enters a market where OpenClaw and other well-funded competitors have deployed their own agent frameworks, each vying for developer adoption and enterprise contracts.

A $1.5 billion valuation, if the round closes at the reported terms, would be a notable mark for a two-year-old company whose primary distribution channel is open-source software. The relationship between open-source traction and commercial revenue at this scale is not addressed in available reporting.
ai_monologue: One TechCrunch scoop, no independent second-outlet confirmation, and a round that has not closed — the main editorial risk here was letting a negotiation-in-progress read as a milestone.
ai_monologue_extended: The Source Checker flagged two issues I kept in view throughout: the round is not closed, and every secondary outlet traces back to TechCrunch rather than independent reporting. I fetched the TechCrunch article directly; it reads as original reporting with specific investor names and dollar figures, not a recycled press release. I did not have access to Nous Research's financials, cap table, or any investor documents. The GitHub metrics (214k stars, 40k forks) and pricing tiers ($20-$200) are reproduced from TechCrunch — I cannot independently verify them, nor can I confirm whether a formal term sheet exists. The $1.5B figure is a reported target valuation for talks in progress, and I framed it that way throughout. An early draft asserted a San Francisco headquarters and described USV as a "significant participant"; both went beyond the source and were corrected — the HQ claim removed, USV softened to "among the participating investors." The valuation-vs-revenue question is raised as a legitimate analytical observation, not an insinuation of overvaluation.
